job.title: HR Business Partner 6 Month FTC! $210K - $230K Package
job.description:
The Organisation

Levyl is partnering with a large, complex and geographically dispersed organisation to appoint two experienced People & Culture Business Partners for an initial six-month fixed-term contract.

The organisation is progressing through a significant transformation program involving changes to its workforce, and operating structure. Consultation is already underway across multiple business areas, creating the need for additional business partnering capability during a critical period of change.

This is an opportunity to contribute to a meaningful and complex transformation program while working closely with senior leaders and an experienced People & Culture function.

The Team

Reporting to the Head of People Business Partners, you will join an established team of approximately six Business Partners located across NSW.

The team is experienced, collaborative and accustomed to working within a complex industrial environment. While each Business Partner is responsible for a designated portfolio, the team regularly shares knowledge, works through issues together and provides support across business areas when required.

You will be trusted to manage your portfolio with autonomy while remaining closely connected to the wider team through regular meetings and ongoing collaboration.

The Opportunity

As a People & Culture Business Partner, you will take ownership of a designated business portfolio and work closely with executives, senior leaders and employees.

The role will combine significant organisational change activity with broader operational business partnering. A key focus will be guiding leaders through workforce consultation, and union engagement while ensuring agreed activity continues to progress in line with the appropriate obligations and timeframes.

Your role will be to guide, coach and support leaders through the required processes while carefully managing the impact on employees.
Specific responsibilities will include:
  • Supporting leaders through organisational change, consultation and workforce realignment
  • Managing union engagement and formal consultation requirements
  • Interpreting and applying Enterprise Agreement provisions and relevant industrial instruments
  • Coaching leaders through sensitive decisions and challenging conversations
  • Ensuring agreed change activity progresses effectively and within required timeframes
  • Managing employee relations matters, complaints and workplace investigations as required
  • Providing advice across performance, workforce planning and organisational design
  • Supporting general People & Culture queries and day-to-day business partnering matters
  • Collaborating with employee relations and other specialist People & Culture teams
The opportunities are open to candidates located across NSW, with some planned travel potentially required depending on business needs, but mostly you will work remotely. 

About You

Levyl is looking for accomplished People & Culture Business Partners who can quickly understand a complex operating environment, establish credibility and provide confident support with minimal direction within a unionised environment.

You will bring substantial end-to-end business partnering experience, including direct involvement in organisational change, workforce consultation and industrial relations. Experience working with unions and independently interpreting Enterprise Agreements is essential.

Experience gained within utilities, infrastructure, government, local council, manufacturing or another operational and highly unionised environment will be highly regarded. Industry experience is less important than demonstrated success supporting complex change within an Enterprise Agreement-covered workforce. Along with this, a practical and proactive working style will be critical! You will know which questions to ask, where to find the information you need and when to bring the right people together to progress an issue.

The Process

This opportunity is being managed confidentially by Levyl. The interview process will include an initial meeting with a Levyl team member, followed by one or two meetings with the organisation’s senior People & Culture leaders.
For a confidential discussion, please contact Emilia Rodriguez on 0497 938 177 or emilia@levyl.com.au.

Levyl encourages diverse, equitable and inclusive recruitment solutions and is committed to responding to every applicant. We make selection and shortlist decisions based on your skills, experience, personal attributes and motivators. When applying for one of our advertised opportunities, please share the pronouns you use and any reasonable adjustments you may require throughout the interview process.

job.title: HR Business Partner
job.description:
The Organisation

Levyl is partnering with an established, privately owned Australian organisation to appoint a People & Culture Business Partner.

With a diverse portfolio of businesses and an evolving people agenda, the organisation is focused on strengthening learning and development, improving the employee experience and continuing to modernise its ways of working. It offers a collaborative and fast-moving environment where relationships matter, ideas are welcomed and the People & Culture team has genuine scope to influence business outcomes.

This is an opportunity to join a values-led organisation with a strong history, clear ambitions for the future and an appetite to continue improving its people practices, systems and frameworks.

The Team

Reporting to an established and collaborative People & Culture Manager, you will work closely with an experienced and collaborative leader who is focused on delivering a practical, progressive and commercially aligned people function.

You will operate as a trusted partner across the business, taking ownership of day-to-day people matters while contributing to broader culture, capability and transformation initiatives. The relationship will offer support and guidance, alongside the autonomy to manage your portfolio, influence leaders and identify better ways of working.

The Opportunity

As the People & Culture Business Partner, you will deliver proactive, practical and employee experience-focused solutions across a diverse stakeholder group.

You will partner with leaders and employees across the full employee lifecycle, balancing hands-on operational delivery with broader organisational priorities. You will coach leaders, manage employee relations matters and contribute to initiatives spanning culture, workforce planning, capability, change and continuous improvement.

Specific responsibilities will include:
  • Partnering with leaders and employees on operational people matters, including employee relations, performance, engagement, policies and processes
  • Providing practical and commercially considered advice across performance management, misconduct, grievances and workplace investigations
  • Coaching leaders to strengthen their capability across communication, feedback, performance and employee engagement
  • Supporting organisational change, business transformation and the implementation of new ways of working
  • Driving employee engagement, workplace wellbeing, inclusion and cultural initiatives
  • Supporting recruitment, onboarding, workforce planning and succession activities
  • Contributing to performance, talent review and leadership development programs
  • Identifying capability gaps and facilitating relevant learning and development initiatives
  • Using people data, workforce trends and insights to inform decision-making
  • Improving P&C systems, processes and frameworks to create a more streamlined employee experience
  • Supporting reporting, governance, audit and workplace compliance requirements
About You

We are  looking for a proactive and commercially minded HR generalist with recent experience in a Senior HR Advisor, People & Culture Business Partner or comparable role. Experience gained within manufacturing, hospitality, FMCG or another fast-paced environment will be highly regarded.

The successful candidate will bring broad capability across performance, recruitment, workforce planning and the employee lifecycle, alongside a genuine interest in culture, capability, change and process improvement.

A practical approach to problem-solving, strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to adapt to different individuals and situations will be key. Credibility will come through thoughtful advice, sound judgement and a willingness to take ownership.

This opportunity will appeal to someone who enjoys working within an evolving organisation and contributing ideas that improve existing practices. Experience supporting organisational change, leadership development, HR systems or cultural initiatives will be highly regarded.

The Process

job.description:

Our client is part of one of Australia’s largest FMCG organisations, with a significant national footprint and a large, diverse workforce.
Operating across a multi-site environment, the business has a strong focus on investing in its people and building the leadership and workforce capability required to support its ongoing success. As the OD Manager, you will play an important role in delivering key organisational development, talent and capability priorities across the business.

You will take ownership of the program through assessment, resource mobilisation and site readiness, ensuring there is a clear plan, strong governance and continued momentum through to implementation. Alongside this, you will contribute to broader organisational development priorities, with a particular focus on talent reviews and leadership development.

  • Coordinate site assessments and readiness activities across multiple locations
  • Mobilise the people and resources required to support successful program delivery
  • Coordinate induction, training deployment and broader learning activities as the program progresses
  • Support the recruitment and onboarding of regional training resources
  • Establish effective program governance and provide clear updates to senior stakeholders
  • Partner closely with People & Culture, operational leaders and site teams to understand capability requirements and translate these into action
  • Lead and support talent review processes and development initiatives
  • Contribute to the delivery of leadership development programs

You will be an experienced Organisational Development professional with a strong background across talent, learning and capability, coupled with demonstrated experience delivering complex people programs.
